To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sensitivity of ATPase to 11 different inhibitors varied through the cell cycle in a manner suggesting similarities and differences in the binding sites for the inhibitors.

the ATPase of S. pombe is regulated by the cell cycle in a way that is similar to the regulation of mitochondrial ATPase in mammalian cells, and the ATPase of the yeast is inhibited by a number of inhibitors of mitochondrial ATPase that act on different binding sites, and the binding sites are expressed in a cell cycle-regulated manner.
the ATPase activity of S. pombe is regulated during the cell cycle and that different inhibitors of ATPase show different sensitivities to inhibition at different stages of cell growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the cell cycle in fission yeast.
the study of the regulation of energy metabolism and the control of the cell cycle in fission yeast.
the regulation of the activity of the mitochondrial membrane-bound adenosine tri-phosphatase (ATPase) of Schizosacharomyces pombe (the fission yeast).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ATPase of S. pombe is not homogeneous, but is made up of at least four distinct components, each with its own characteristic inhibitor-binding site(s).
there are at least four different sites on the ATPase complex of Schizosacharomyces pombe, each of which is expressed at different times during the cell cycle.
, although the mitochondrial ATPase of S. pombe shows similarities with the ATPase of higher organisms in many respects, there is also evidence of some fundamental differences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitochondrial ATPase of S. pombe shows a number of similarities and differences in the binding of inhibitors to the various sites during the cell-cycle progression.
the cell cycle is a complex programme in which the expression of genes for the various proteins of the mitochondrial ATPase is coordinated with other aspects of the life cycle.
there is no single binding site for any of the inhibitors tested, and that there are two distinct classes of inhibitor, one of which includes those acting on Fo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a lot of variation in the expression of different inhibitor-binding sites during cell-cycle progression, and that this is a reflection of the changes in membrane structure that occur during this process.
the cell cycle has a profound impact on the activity of the mitochondria.
the cell cycle is an extremely important determinant of the sensitivity of the mitochondrial membrane ATPase to inhibitors of energy conservation.
